answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake and keep a verifiable service history before it earns full trust. Forging hundreds of fake identities then costs real capital and time, since each one must stake, serve, and wait. Like a gale funneling ships through a narrow inlet, the stake-and-history gate concentrates attackers at one costly bottleneck, while a small honest island of established agents vouches for newcomers only by risking their own standing.
